notes.title: UPDATE 1.0.3 WITH PATCH NOTES
notes.content:
Greetings Warrior, 

Good job. We’ve heard that you’ve been working hard to prevent Lemonkus from wiping out mankind. 

The development team heard your requests and is now proud to deploy its brand-new patch bringing enhancement into the current gameplay with few improvements, as well as fixing issues that impacted players’ experience. And most of all, Input rebinding is now possible from the title screen menu.  

Check out the changelog detailed below : 

[b]Features and Balancing [/b]

[*] Input rebinding is now possible from the title screen menu
[*] A wifi router has been added to the SSD Floatanic 
[*] The last switch climb in the SSD Floatanic has been made easier 
[*] The question mark marker will only get removed when you have the power core and enter the mech room 

[b]Visual fixes [/b]

[*] In the caves, the initial lava room will not show the opening in the bottom left on the map anymore. 

[b]Audio Fixes [/b]

[*] ZenGuy’s missile sounds volume are now respecting SFX slider 
[*] Lemonkus’ laser fist will now respect SFX slider 
[*] Low energy sound will stop playing when you kill the final boss

[b]Gameplay fixes and improvement [/b]

[*] Added a forced delay to the cinematic skip of 1.5 seconds in between to fix various ‘too fast skip’ issues. 
[*] Added a first hat unlocked achievement
[*] You can no longer pause the game right after loading which can look like the game froze 
[*] Katana charge attack fixes to avoid glitching through the world 
[*] Store categories are now properly labeled with ‘?????’ if you do not have the weapon yet 
[*] Fixed the Disconnected Woods sometimes having random result 
[*] Furious Ferro’s babby fluids will get destroyed now when you kill Ferro 
[*] Fixed moving through the lava opening before hitting the switch in the cave 
[*] ZenGuy’s missiles are now immune to the Katana’s charge attack 
[*] Removed hidden spikes in the Church of Skebin trial 
[*] Fixed an issue where the Captain’s Hat was sometimes not obtainable 
[*] Fixed an issue where the dialogue of the Zensei after killing him could softlock the game 
[*] Fixed the Robopolis treasure chest counter not showing the correct amount
[*] Fixed rocks around a dash bar in the desert which possibly made Tabby clip with the terrain 
[*] Installing the exploit from the router in the final level and quitting during the transition will now properly save you at the next spawn point 

Exhilarating battles await you. See you on the battleground!

KUNAI came out three weeks ago and we can’t thank you enough for playing the game, sharing your love for Tabby, reporting bugs, creating fanart and speedrunning like a true ninja! 

We're currently working on our first patch which will have a lot of bugfixes (including the going out of bounds due to the charge attack, sorry about that ːsteamfacepalmː) and improves the overall experience of playing the game! 

It's been a lot of fun seeing all the fanart popping up over the past month so we figured we'd highlight some! (ps: please keep them coming, we do print them all out and hang them on our wall at the office).

Follow [url=https://twitter.com/nazuna32/status/1227566145844043777]Nazuna32 here[/url]

[h2]Tabby Love <3[/h2]
Everyone loves Tabby's expressions and I think 黒いスズメ loves them too! Can we just sit for a minute and appreciate how cute and expressive the face of this tablet is?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34329396/293c3be82b5138af9f78b5c866077dbbd2acf688.jpg[/img]

[h2]Speedrun records![/h2]
We could not imagine the game would be completable under an hour let alone at a staggering 24 minutes by [url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCeeH8t4QnHRUV_P153ZEPdg]seanpr[/url]! It is in the category where glitches are permitted, but still...

Have you beaten the trial in the Church of Skebin yet? If you have, you might want to go back to try and beat Skebin's personal record at a crazy 14.37 seconds! Yes he's an actual person and is determined to keep his own record for his names sake. Check out his fastest run to date below:

[h2]See you soon[/h2]
Keep the art and records coming, we can't get enough of them! And most of all enjoy the game and let us know if you have any suggestions in the comments! If you want to stay up to date you can do one of the following:

Join us in our official [url=https://discord.gg/X7vufTb]KUNAI discord[/url]
Follow us on twitter [url=https://twitter.com/turtleblaze]@TurtleBlaze[/url] 
Follow our publisher on twitter [url=https://twitter.com/turtleblaze]@thearcadecrew[/url]

notes.title: Kunai proves anyone can be a ninja, even an iPad
notes.content:
I am a simple creature, easily amused by flashing lights and bleepy noises, so I’m always up for a good metroidvania. Bonus points if it has some clever-looking movement tricks, bouncy mid-air combat and it’s just icing on the cake if there’s a grappling hook, too. Kunai, from TurtleBlaze, looks like it ticks each and every one of those boxes, plus the hidden bonus one of having a fun setting. A post-apocalyptic, post-human world populated by weird robots made out of junk. Protagonist Tabby may have the soul of a warrior, but he has the face of an iPad. Take a peek at the debut trailer below.

(more…)

notes.title: Save humanity in this side-scrolling action-platformer about a touchscreen ninja
notes.content:
Kunai is a tablet-powered side-scrolling ninja parkour hack-and-slash open-world Metroidvania, and when I say "tablet-powered" I don't mean that it's played on a tablet. (This is PC Gamer, after all.) I mean that the lead character, for reasons I don't fully (or even begin to) understand, is literally a tablet. 

Tabby, as our touchscreen warrior is properly named, must save what remains of humanity from extinction at the hands of an out-of-control AI by running, jumping, grappling, and chopping an assortment of evil consumer electronics into small component bits. Players will unlock and upgrade special abilities, weapons, and "kickass ninja tricks," and traverse a world filled with secrets and strange characters. 

The action looks plentiful—the sort of high-speed, fast-reflex nonsense I am terrible at—but it's also very cute, which is what caught my eye: The washed-out colors nicely emphasize Kunai's retro visual style, and Tabby has a warm, lovable smile (when he's not, you know, murdering things). There's no release date yet but I would expect something relatively soon, as Kunai (which, by the way, is a Japanese farming tool from the Tensho Era that was later adopted as a weapon most commonly associated with ninja) will be playable next week at GDC, and then the week after that at PAX East. For those who aren't attending either, it's listed on Steam and there's a website up at kunaigame.com.
